transcript.content: Hello, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came in because my mind keeps going blank, especially at work. I’ll be looking at the road-closure forms or holding the stop-slow paddle, and suddenly I just can’t remember the steps I’ve done for years. It’s been happening at bad times, and it’s really worrying me.
During these blank moments, do you lose awareness of what’s happening around you?

I don’t think I lose awareness, exactly. It’s more like my mind just blanks out. I’m still there, I can see the forms or the paddle, but suddenly I can’t remember what I’m supposed to do next, even though I’ve done it for years.
During these blank moments, do you make any repetitive movements like lip-smacking, picking at things, or staring fixedly?
I haven’t noticed anything like that, no. I might just stand there and stare at what I’m doing because I’m trying to figure it out, but I don’t think I’m smacking my lips or picking at things.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?
Yes. Most mornings I wake up feeling really heavy and sad, like there’s this hollow feeling in my chest. It’s like the day already feels ruined before I even get out of bed.
Have you lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

Yes. I used to be really involved with things—like organizing rides for choir, setting up garden swaps, helping with snacks for youth basketball. Now I’ll just sit for hours staring at my phone, and I don’t even feel like answering people. It’s like the interest or the push to do it is just gone.
Have these low mood feelings been present nearly every day for at least two weeks?
Yes, it’s been pretty much every day. Most mornings I wake up with that heavy, hollow sadness in my chest, like the day is already ruined before I even get out of bed.
Do these blank moments tend to happen when you’re feeling especially anxious or worried?

Not always anxiety, no. It’s more like my mind just shuts off at the worst time. I’ll be looking at road-closure forms, or even holding the stop-slow paddle, and suddenly I can’t remember the steps I’ve done for years. It scares me because I should know what to do, but it just goes blank.
Do these blank moments ever happen when your mood feels okay?

Yes. Before the depression got really bad, there were a few weeks where I was still going to work and church, like functioning on the outside, but I was already having those moments. I’d hear my name when nobody was there, and I started thinking signs or even the radio were sending messages about me. So it wasn’t only when my mood was at its worst.
Was there ever a period of at least two weeks when you were hearing your name or believing messages were about you while your mood was not depressed?

Yes. Before the depression got really deep, there were several weeks where I was still getting myself to work and going to church, but I was already hearing my name when no one was there. I was also thinking signs and the radio were sending messages about me. My mood wasn’t as low then.
Have you ever had a convulsion or seizure where your whole body shook?
No, I don’t think so. I’ve never had my whole body shake like that, at least not that I know of.
When you were hearing your name or thinking the radio or signs were sending messages about you, were you feeling depressed at that time?

Yes. For many months, it’s been during the same stretch where I’ve been waking up sad and feeling guilty. I wasn’t eating much, and a lot of mornings I’d wish I just wouldn’t wake up. The voices and the messages from trucks or the radio were happening along with that.

When you heard your name or felt the radio or signs were sending messages about you, did those experiences make you feel that you deserved punishment or that something bad was going to happen because of you?

Yes. When that happens, I start thinking it means I did something wrong. I keep going over every little thing I failed at—with my friend, with the choir, with my family—and it feels like I’m useless and that I deserve whatever punishment is coming.

Psychotic symptoms are present, including hearing their name and ideas/referential beliefs that signs, trucks, and the radio were sending messages.
